definitions: The supreme law of the United States of America.
It is the foundation of the U.S. federal government and serves as the blueprint for the legal and political organization of the country.
It outlines the framework for the three branches of government (legislative, executive, and judicial) and establishes the rights and freedoms of American citizens.
examples: The U.S. Constitution was ratified in 1788.
Amendments to the U.S. Constitution require a two-thirds vote.
Many legal arguments reference the U.S. Constitution.
